title: Miketz: it is not in me (Genesis 41:16)
hook: Joseph tells Pharaoh the meaning comes from God, not from him

segments.voice: Yesterday, Miketz: two full years of waiting, then out of the dungeon in a day. Your line was it ends suddenly. What did you do to be ready? Today, Joseph stands before Pharaoh. Day two hundred seven.

You finally get the meeting with the big boss. Or the audition. Or the chance to pitch the idea to the person who can make it happen. And they say: I hear you're the one who can do this. It's the moment to shine. To say, yes, that's me. Joseph has just been pulled out of the dungeon, shaved and changed. He's standing in the court of the most powerful man in the world, a prisoner one hour ago. Pharaoh says: I've had a dream, and I've heard that you can read dreams. Today: it is not in me.
screen: `THE BIG MEETING.` → `I HEAR YOU'RE THE ONE.` → `A PRISONER BEFORE PHARAOH.`

segments.voice: Joseph's first words to Pharaoh, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace." In Hebrew, the first part is a single word, biladai. Not me. Apart from me. Think about the risk of saying that. Joseph needs Pharaoh to think he's valuable. He has one shot to get out of prison for good. And the first thing he does is hand the credit away. Remember the young Joseph, seventeen, telling his brothers about his dreams, where their sheaves bowed down to his? That Joseph talked a lot about himself. This one, after the pit and the prison, talks about God. And he keeps doing it. Pharaoh tells both dreams, the cows and the ears of grain, and Joseph says: God has told Pharaoh what he is about to do. Seven years of plenty, seven years of famine. The dream came twice because the thing is fixed by God, and God will do it soon. Again and again, in front of a king who is himself treated as divine, Joseph names his own God. And here's the surprise. Giving the credit away doesn't make him smaller. Pharaoh looks around his court and asks: could we find anyone like this, a man with the spirit of God in him? And he puts Joseph over all of Egypt. The rabbis prized this. The Mishnah says that whoever repeats a teaching in the name of the one who said it brings redemption into the world. Say where things came from. Don't take what isn't yours.
screen: `BILADAI: NOT ME.` · `THE BOY WHO TALKED ABOUT HIMSELF.` · `GOD HAS TOLD PHARAOH.` · `SAY IT IN THE NAME OF WHO SAID IT.` · then, large: `IT IS NOT IN ME.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: give credit away once. Settle, and breathe. Think of something you're proud of lately. A good result at work, a meal, a kid who's doing well, a hard day you got through. Now trace it back. Who taught you? Who helped? What was given to you that you didn't make yourself? If you pray, you can thank God for it. Either way, choose one person you could name out loud. The bell holds the time.
Miketz. At the end: the portion where Joseph, before Pharaoh, says the meaning isn't in him, but comes from God.
Your line: not in me. Today, when someone praises you for something, name one person, or one gift, that made it possible. Day two hundred seven.

howItsDone: Jewish learning takes care to cite who said what, and students repeat teachings in the name of the teacher who first taught them, following the Mishnah's saying about bringing redemption.

original.note: Hebrew: not me, apart from me. Joseph's first word to Pharaoh.

trapdoor: what you thought: Joseph being modest.
what it means: in his one chance to impress a king, he gives the credit to God.
what a scholar hears: Mishnah Avot 6:6 says whoever repeats a thing in the name of its speaker brings redemption, learning it from Esther naming Mordecai.

notes: Genesis 41:38 paraphrased ('a man with the spirit of God in him').
Mishnah Avot 6:6 (in the name of its speaker; Esther 2:22) from memory; confirm.
'A king who is himself treated as divine' describes Egyptian royal ideology generally; confirm framing.
The contrast between the young Joseph and the later Joseph is a common teaching; confirm.
